case.label: B
case.text: Inspector also produces network-related findings (network reachability), so a hurried candidate could argue it reports risky network paths of an instance; but reachability describes possible exposure, not actual communication with known malicious IP addresses, which is threat-intelligence detection in GuardDuty. Options A, B and D share the same organization and delegated-administrator wording, so only the service choice decides; no wording cue gives D away.

case.label: D
case.text: A Lambda function with a card-number regular expression does identify the objects and can run daily, so it meets the functional requirement; it loses only on operational overhead (cross-account access, scaling over many objects, false positives without checksum validation). Option C does not say how a Macie job reaches buckets in several accounts (it needs the Macie administrator account), but no other option handles the multi-account part better, so the missing detail does not create a second answer.

case.label: D
case.text: Security Hub CSPM has a PCI DSS standard and its control findings are evidence for a PCI audit, so D sounds relevant; but those findings describe the company's own resource configuration, and the stem explicitly says the auditor wants the AWS SOC 2 report and the AWS PCI DSS attestation for AWS's own controls and reviews the company's controls separately. The stem closes this gap well.

case.label: B
case.text: CloudTrail event history keeps 90 days of management events and 'three months ago' sits right at that edge, so a candidate could argue the AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress and RevokeSecurityGroupIngress events still show the changes; but event history shows API calls, not the rule set at a point in time, and rebuilding state would need every change since the group was created. Wording cue: the stem itself says the company recorded configuration with AWS Config, and option A echoes it ('configuration history', 'configuration item'), which makes A easy to spot; consider saying 'six months ago' to remove the 90-day edge case entirely.

case.label: C
case.text: Detective ingests GuardDuty findings and groups related findings into finding groups, so it can look like a central list; but it is an investigation tool, it does not take Inspector and Macie findings as one prioritized list, and it does not aggregate across Regions. Option D says 'AWS Security Hub' while other items say 'Security Hub CSPM'; both the new Security Hub and Security Hub CSPM ingest these three services and support cross-Region aggregation, so the naming does not create a second answer, but keep the naming consistent across the chapter.

case.label: C
case.text: GuardDuty Runtime Monitoring watches processes on EC2 instances, so a candidate could argue it notices a bad package at run time; but GuardDuty detects threats and suspicious behavior, not known CVEs in installed software packages, which is Inspector's vulnerability scanning. The twin of this item (malicious IP communication) uses the same options, so the pair tests the decision cleanly.

case.label: C
case.text: A Config rule 'in proactive mode' sounds like prevention, so a candidate could pick it for the Block Public Access requirement; but proactive evaluation checks resource definitions before deployment when called (for example through CloudFormation hooks) and does not block an API call from an administrator or root user, while an SCP on the organization root applies to member-account root users. Option D does not say Config is enabled in every account, but A, the only other option for the logging part, is clearly heavier, so the pair D and E stays unique.

case.label: B
case.text: Athena over CloudTrail logs gives exactly the source IP addresses and API calls of the role and is a common root-cause method; it loses on development effort (writing queries) and the stem never says a trail delivers logs to S3. The stem states Detective has run for a year, which removes the 'not enough history' objection; 'LEAST development effort' is the deciding constraint and it is present.

case.label: C
case.text: Option C ends with GuardDuty enabled too, so it would also detect compromised instances and stolen credentials; it is wrong only because GuardDuty reads its foundational data sources (CloudTrail management events, VPC flow logs, DNS logs) through independent streams without the customer turning those logs on, so C adds work and delay. The stem's 'no CloudTrail trail and no VPC flow logs' is the deliberate trap and 'as soon as possible' plus 'LEAST operational overhead' decide it.

case.label: C
case.text: Security Hub CSPM is the central place for findings, so a candidate could believe it keeps them as long as needed; but it also keeps findings for a limited period (90 days), not 2 years, and option A fails because GuardDuty finding retention is fixed, not a setting. The stem names the existing central S3 bucket, which points to D; that is a fair hint, not a giveaway.

case.label: C
case.text: A Lambda antivirus function on each upload meets the malware requirement and gives a result before processing; it loses only because the company prefers fully managed services and it needs daily definition updates, while GuardDuty Malware Protection for S3 scans new uploads and tags the result. Option A is the trap that Macie scans for malware; option B could also be met by Macie automated sensitive data discovery, but that is not offered, so no second answer arises.

case.label: B
case.text: Cross-Region aggregation does bring us-west-2 findings into the us-east-1 view, so a candidate who thinks the findings exist but are not visible could pick B; but the stem says no findings appear at all, and aggregation only copies findings that already exist, while CSPM controls need AWS Config recording in the same Region to evaluate resources. The stem gives the deciding fact directly ('records ... with AWS Config in us-east-1 only'), which is a strong cue but also the necessary constraint.
